I am 78 years old. My hands know this land better than any paper could tell me. My children are in the city now — my son comes back during harvest if I ask him. I have 3 mu of flat land, same land my husband farmed before he passed. I cannot carry much anymore, so I keep things simple.

I will do what I have always done here in Quzhou: wheat in the ground after the autumn, corn after the wheat comes off in June. Every family here does this. The land expects it. I tried cotton once, many years ago — too much work, too much spraying. I will not do that again.

For wheat, I will go to the village supply store and buy the seed they sell — the improved kind, not the old seeds I used to save. The store seed grows better, everyone switched years ago. I will hire old Zhang's son to bring his rotary tiller. I will spread compound fertilizer when I plant, then in March when the wheat starts to wake up I will scatter urea by hand over the field. I will water twice: once before the ground freezes, once in spring. I will spray for weeds in early spring, and maybe once more if I see something wrong with the leaves.

After wheat harvest, I will plant corn. Hybrid seed only — nobody uses the old kind anymore. Same tilling, same neighbor's machine. Summer usually brings enough rain here but I will water once if it stays dry in July. I put fertilizer down at planting and a little more when the corn is knee-high.

3 mu is all I can manage. I will not try to do more and hurt myself.
